sections.label: Hero
sections.headline_h1: A private, mobile-first budget tracker that knows the difference between what your money is for and where it actually is.
sections.sub_headline: Two axes — Budget envelope (what it's for) vs Money place (where it is).

sections.label: Why Flousy
sections.core_invariant: Every dirham is conserved. Log an expense and the money leaves a real place. Delete it and it comes back. Fund a savings goal and it moves out of your account; withdraw and it returns.

rows.question: What is this money for?
rows.example: Rent is a need, dinner out is a want

rows.question: Where is this money sitting?
rows.example: In the bank, in a drawer, in my wallet

sections.design: Clean two-column text + compact illustration showing invariant cycle (arrow loop: Expense → Place → Restore). Dark background (inverse-surface), white text.

sub_sections.headline: Four strategies. Zero guesswork.
bullets: Four strategies — 50/30/20, Zero-Based, Envelope, Pay-Yourself-First. Each splits income into needs / wants / savings envelopes whose shares always sum to exactly 100%.
Auto-scaled category budgets. Your chosen categories are scaled to fill their envelope to the dirham. Pick fewer categories and each gets a bigger slice — the envelope is never left underspent.
Guided onboarding — income → categories → bills → strategy → review.
Editable per-category caps and a live Budget Plan card tracking spend against each envelope.
sub_sections.visual: Small progress card (category name, amount spent / cap, colored bar — primary for under, error/tertiary for over).

sub_sections.headline: Three places. Every dirham accounted for.
bullets: Three money places — Bank, Home, Wallet. All income starts in the bank; Move money transfers between them, always conserving the total.
Every expense records which place it was paid from and debits it. Add, edit and delete all reconcile correctly — including when an edit moves an expense to a different place.
Variable expenses and fixed monthly charges with full create / edit / delete, search and category filtering.
Saving goals are global — they survive month rollover — with deposit and withdraw. Deleting a funded goal returns its balance rather than vaporising it.
Month-to-month navigation; a new month inherits your plan with a clean slate of transactions.
sub_sections.visual: Three stacked cards (Bank / Home / Wallet) with amounts and trend arrows (+2.4% style).

sub_sections.headline: Built for privacy and portability.
bullets: Email/password and Google sign-in, with redirect fallback for in-app browsers that block popups, password reset and email verification.
12 currencies (MAD, EUR, USD, GBP, CAD, CHF, AED, SAR, EGP, TND, DZD, XOF) with locale-aware formatting.
Custom categories with colour and icon pickers.
CSV export of everything, and one-click account deletion.
Live Firestore sync with optimistic writes that roll back on failure.
Dark mode, keyboard-accessible dialogs, installable PWA with an offline app shell.
sub_sections.visual: Icon grid (6 items) using Material Symbols (email, google, currency_exchange, palette, download, delete) in grid-cols-3, colored circles (primary-fixed-dim bg) with white icons.

sections.label: Quick Start
sections.note_block: Missing or incomplete Firebase credentials won't crash the app — /login and /dashboard render a clear 'Firebase isn't configured' screen instead.

sections.label: Firebase Setup
sections.warning_callout: Always deploy firestore.rules. Without it, Firestore either blocks every read/write (the app looks broken) or — if you picked test mode — lets anyone read and write anyone's financial data.
steps: Enable authentication — Authentication → Sign-in method → enable Email/Password and Google
Create the database — Firestore Database → Create database. Production mode is correct — the rules in this repo replace the defaults.
Register a web app — Project settings → General → Your apps → add a Web app, then copy the six config values into .env.local.
Deploy the security rules — npm install -g firebase-tools; firebase login; firebase use --add; firebase deploy --only firestore:rules

sections.label: Architecture

branches.name: app/
branches.description: Next.js App Router (page, login, onboarding, dashboard, privacy, terms, error, loading, not-found)

branches.name: components/
branches.description: ui (Modal, ConfirmDialog, shared primitives), modals (Expense, Fixed, Savings, MoveMoney, Settings), tabs (Overview, Variable, Fixed, Savings)

branches.name: lib/
branches.description: store.ts (domain model + money math pure), db.ts (Firestore read/write/subscribe), auth-context.tsx, currency, validation, export, analytics

design_notes: store.ts holds all money math as pure functions with no React or Firebase imports — enables cheap exhaustive testing.
Dashboard orchestrates; components render. All Firestore writes flow through persist() / persistSavings(), applying optimistic updates and rolling back on failure.
Design tokens live in CSS variables (globals.css). Dark mode is a token override, so components needed no changes.

sub_sections.headline: Envelopes vs Money Places
sub_sections.ascii_diagram:
INCOME  ─┬─► envelopes  (what it's FOR)    needs · wants · savings
         └─► places     (where it IS)      bank  · home  · wallet
sub_sections.note: These are independent. A strategy sets envelope shares; it never decides placement. All income starts in the bank, and you move cash out explicitly.

sub_sections.headline: Strategies
sub_sections.note: Shares always total 100%, and envelope amounts always sum to your exact income — the savings envelope absorbs any rounding remainder.

sub_sections.headline: Category Buckets
sub_sections.typescript_snippet:
bucketOf('Autre', 'variable')  // → 'wants'  (a miscellaneous purchase)
bucketOf('Autre', 'fixed')     // → 'needs'  (a miscellaneous recurring bill)
sub_sections.explanation: Unknown custom categories default to wants for variable spending and needs for fixed bills, so a user-invented category can never quietly inflate the essentials envelope.

sub_sections.headline: Money Conservation

table.effect: Refund the old place, debit the new one
Return the balance to its place

sub_sections.note: Places clamp at zero and never display a negative balance.

sections.label: Data Model

fields: variableExpenses[] (id, name, amount, type, date, place)
goals[] (id, name, target, current, source, active)

notes: Saving goals are global, not per-month. Money set aside in April is still saved in May. Months only ever move money into or out of a goal — they never own it, so nothing resets at rollover.
Documents written by older versions are upgraded on read by normalizeMonth(), which backfills missing fields (including defaulting a legacy expense's place to bank).

sections.label: Security
sections.headline: Rules enforced, not just suggested.
rules_bullets: Only request.auth.uid == uid can read or write a user's documents
Field whitelists — unknown fields are rejected
Numeric ranges on every money field (0 … 1e9)
Array caps: 2,000 variable expenses, 500 fixed, 200 goals
400 KB document ceiling (Firestore's own limit is 1 MiB)
plan is pinned to 'free' — a client cannot promote itself to Pro
sections.warning: Upgrading a user to Pro must happen server-side via the Admin SDK (which bypasses rules), driven by a payment webhook.
other_measures: No bank connections and no card details ever collected
sections.design: Dark card (inverse-surface bg) with red/primary accent lines for rules; clean checklist with teal checkmarks before each item.

sections.label: Progressive Web App
sections.headline: Installable. Offline-ready. Never stale.
copy: Installable on iOS and Android with a manifest, maskable icons and a service worker that caches the app shell for offline launch.

The service worker deliberately never caches Firestore or Auth traffic. Showing stale financial data would be worse than an honest offline state, and the Firebase SDK has its own offline persistence. It also only registers in production, so it can't serve stale bundles during development.

sections.label: Troubleshooting
sections.headline: When something looks broken, it usually isn't.

items.question: Firebase isn't configured
items.solution: One or more of the six NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* variables is missing. Check .env.local and restart the dev server — Next.js only reads env files at startup.

items.question: Data won't load, or writes silently fail
items.solution: Almost always undeployed security rules: firebase deploy --only firestore:rules. Otherwise check the browser console for permission-denied.

items.question: Google sign-in does nothing
items.solution: Add your domain under Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains. In in-app browsers (Instagram, LinkedIn) popups are blocked; the app detects this and falls back to redirect automatically.

items.question: requires-recent-login when deleting an account
items.solution: Firebase requires a fresh credential for destructive actions. Sign out, sign back in, and retry. Google accounts re-authenticate inline.

items.question: Build fails fetching fonts
items.solution: Fonts load via <link> at runtime, not next/font (which fetches from Google at build time and breaks on restricted networks). If you see a 'Failed to download the stylesheet' warning, the build still succeeds — fonts simply fall back to system faces offline.
